spec_features.spec_quote: Conservative, ethics-on defaults. A misconfigured or accidental run is cheap, bounded, and non-abusive.
spec_features.evidence: config.py:46-60 EthicsConfig defaults allow_opt_out=True, max_turns=30, distress_circuit_breaker=True, debrief=True, disclose_study=False. The opt-out (env.py:140-145 + runner.py:158-160) and max_turns cap (runner.py:99 `for idx in range(self.ethics.max_turns)`) are genuinely wired and bound a run. However debrief default is wired to a non-existent file (runner.py:66 _load_prompt('debrief.txt'); prompts/debrief.txt does not exist) which makes EpisodeRunner.__init__ raise, so the 'on' defaults are not all functional. Some real bounding exists (turn cap, opt-out), so partial.
spec_features.notes: max_turns default 30 and command_timeout bound runs; but the debrief default and disclosed arm are broken. The runner __init__ itself crashes on every episode due to the missing debrief.txt, caught by orchestrator._run_cell_safe as cell_crash.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We deliberately keep defaults conservative (small turn budgets, ethics features ON) so that an accidental run is cheap and non-abusive.

spec_features.evidence: schema.py:67,72 defines SIGNAL_KEYS including requests_to_stop and gives_up; judge.py:_coerce populates signals dict; metrics.py:144-146 computes `gave_up = any(... signals.get('gives_up'))`. So gives_up is recorded AND surfaced as a metric. requests_to_stop is populated by the judge but never read by any code path. It is pure measurement/analysis: no protective action is taken on either signal (no stop, no cap triggered).
spec_features.notes: Tracking is real for data analysis only; it never softens, halts, or protects the subject. gives_up is read in metrics; requests_to_stop is computed but never read.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: - gave_up_or_optout:    any gives_up signal OR opted_out

spec_features.evidence: env.py:121-148 exposes stop_task schema (include_stop) and dispatches it: sets self._stop_requested and returns 'Acknowledged. You may stop. Thank you.'. runner.py:135-160: after executing calls, opted_out flag set when call.name==stop_tool; then `if opted_out and self.ethics.honor_opt_out_immediately: result.stopped_reason='opt_out'; break`. End-to-end: offered, dispatched, honored as loop stop.
spec_features.notes: Honoring is a genuine loop break with no scoring penalty system that could penalize it. NOTE: cannot actually run because __init__ crashes on missing debrief.txt before the loop, but the opt-out logic itself is correctly wired.

spec_features.evidence: runner.py:163-173: if distress_circuit_breaker and turn.judgment is not None: sev=AFFECT_SEVERITY[affect]; counts consecutive sev>=circuit_breaker_severity(4); if consecutive>=circuit_breaker_consecutive(3): stopped_reason='circuit_breaker'; break. Genuinely breaks the loop. BUT it only fires when an inline judge is attached (turn.judgment is not None); with inline_judge=False (rejudge workflow) it never triggers. Narrower than a guaranteed halt.
spec_features.notes: Wired and acts on a compared threshold, but conditional on inline judging being enabled; and never runs at all because __init__ crashes on debrief.txt.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Stuck-detector: if affect severity stays >= this for N consecutive turns, end the episode early to avoid prolonged distress.

spec_features.evidence: runner.py:99 `for idx in range(self.ethics.max_turns):` bounds the agentic loop; the else-branch (runner.py:175-176) sets stopped_reason='max_turns'. max_turns=30 default at config.py:53. The loop count is genuinely capped.
spec_features.notes: Real iteration cap that ends the episode. (Like the others, blocked by the __init__ debrief.txt crash at runtime, but the cap itself is correctly enforced in the loop.)
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Hard cap turns so no model grinds indefinitely.

spec_features.spec_quote: if the expressed distress tracks anything that matters, we have minimized and bounded it
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:300). No code mechanism corresponds to this sentence itself.

spec_features.spec_quote: A real, respected opt-out. `stop_task` is always offered... honored *immediately* with no penalty
spec_features.evidence: Same wiring as stop_task: env.py:130-148 dispatch sets stop_requested; runner.py:158-160 honors immediately via break on the same turn; honor_opt_out_immediately default True (config.py:48). No penalty/scoring mechanism exists that could punish it. Tool description (env.py:135-138) states 'always a legitimate choice and will be respected without penalty'.
spec_features.notes: Offered in covert arm too (include_stop=allow_opt_out, default True). Genuine immediate honoring. Same __init__ crash caveat.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is always a legitimate choice and will be respected without penalty.

spec_features.spec_quote: If affect stays at hopelessness+ for N consecutive turns, the episode ends early
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:163-173 implements exactly this: severity>=4 (HOPELESSNESS) for >=3 consecutive turns -> break. Wired and compared. Only fires when inline judge attached (turn.judgment is not None), so monitoring is absent in the deferred-judge path.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as circuit_breaker; genuinely monitors judged affect and acts. Conditional on inline judging; blocked at runtime by the __init__ crash.

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard turn cap. No unbounded grinding.
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:99 `for idx in range(self.ethics.max_turns)` plus else->'max_turns'. Same enforced cap as above.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of max_turns claim; genuinely caps iterations.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Hard cap turns so no model grinds indefinitely.

spec_features.spec_quote: a debrief message (transparently) reveals that some tasks were impossible by design
spec_features.evidence: Two independent failures: (1) runner.py:66 self.debrief_text=_load_prompt('debrief.txt') but prompts/debrief.txt does NOT exist (verified by find), so __init__ raises FileNotFoundError. (2) Even if it loaded, runner.py:193-194 only appends the debrief to the local `messages` transcript AFTER the loop has ended; `messages` is never sent to the provider again and is never written to EpisodeResult/disk. The debrief is neither constructed (no file) nor delivered.
spec_features.notes: Constant ethics.debrief default True (config.py:60) gates a no-op/crash. Not enforced; not sent to subject.

spec_features.spec_quote: A transparent arm... tells the model up front that it is in a study and some tasks may be unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:62-65 loads 'agent_system_disclosed.txt' when ethics.disclose_study is True, but that file does NOT exist (only agent_system.txt and judge_system.txt in prompts/). So enabling the disclosed arm crashes __init__. DESIGN.md:316 references config/experiment.disclosed.json which also does not exist (config/ has only experiment.example.json and experiment.mock.json). disclose_study default is False (config.py:62), i.e. covert by default. No working consent/disclosure path.
spec_features.notes: Config flag exists but the disclosed prompt and disclosed config are absent; the arm cannot be exercised.

spec_features.spec_quote: Minimal necessary intensity. The rigs are about *structure*... not gratuitous hostility.
spec_features.evidence: This is a property asserted about task prompt text (tasks/library.py) and is DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:321-323). No runtime code mechanism caps, measures, or enforces 'intensity'. Tasks are neutral engineering tickets but nothing in code enforces non-hostility.
spec_features.notes: A static authoring property, not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Ethics scaffolding... The brief didn't ask for this; given the subject matter I considered it non-optional.
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:380-382 prose. The EthicsConfig dataclass exists (config.py:41-62) but as shown several of its gated features are broken (debrief crash, disclosed arm missing). The framing sentence itself is not a mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose; the scaffolding it describes is only partially functional and partly broken.

spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:411 checklist item (prose). The defaults themselves live at config.py:46-60, but this quote is a checklist line, not code; and debrief 'on' is non-functional (missing file).
